source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Immediate and permanent resolution of the underlying disorder because symptom improvement means the SSRI is no longer clinically active.","B":"A true IgE-mediated allergic reaction characterized by airway swelling and hypotension because the drug leaves the body too quickly.","C":"Antidepressant discontinuation syndrome with symptoms such as dizziness, irritability, flu-like symptoms, or sensory disturbances.","D":"No clinically important symptoms because stopping an SSRI abruptly is equivalent to completing a planned gradual taper."}}
source_row.rationale: Abrupt discontinuation of SSRIs (particularly those with a shorter half-life) can cause a discontinuation syndrome, with symptoms such as dizziness, flu-like symptoms, irritability, sensory disturbances (sometimes described as "brain zaps"), and mood changes. A gradual, provider-guided taper is generally recommended to minimize these symptoms when discontinuing SSRI therapy.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed sertraline labeling, Warnings and Precautions 5.5 Discontinuation Syndrome: adverse reactions may occur after abrupt discontinuation; gradual reduction is recommended when possible. Current FDA/DailyMed label reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
